text: You're trying to browse the internet, eager to get to a video or article. But almost every site has that same annoying pop-up.
It demands your attention: 'Accept Cookies,' 'Manage Preferences,' or 'Decline All.' You just want to read, so you quickly click 'Accept.'
You might think these banners are truly about giving you fine-grained control over your data. You try to customize, wading through confusing options.
But for many sites, it's not really about your detailed choices. It's about *proving* they asked. Regulators require websites to obtain consent for data collection.
The simplest design for compliance is to make 'Accept All' the easiest path, often in a prominent warm amber color. Anything else is hidden or complex.
So, you're not choosing privacy; you're helping a website check a legal box. The system isn't designed for your convenience, but for its own protection.
